statement: The pilot admits a uniform explicitly specified finite forcing-bound construction B(r,S).
H_algorithm: Enumerate positive word lengths in increasing order; at each length enumerate every word coloring and every combinatorial line; return the first forcing length.
termination_dependency: Classical finite Hales-Jewett theorem, explicitly used as external established mathematics, not independently re-proved or kernel checked here.
projection: Sum the lattice letters of a word; a word line projects to a+m*S with a the sum of fixed letters and m the positive number of variable positions.
shortcuts: H(1,r)=1; H(k,1)=1; H(2,r)=r by maximal Boolean chains and Hamming-weight lower controls.
acceptance: Written proof covers all finite nonempty S and r>=1, specifies a terminating unbounded mathematical algorithm using the declared classical theorem, and preserves the exact certificate interface. Independently test finite word forcing, avoidance witnesses, binary lengths, lattice extraction and explicit resource refusals.
falsifier: A certified word length fails a finite coloring, a projected line is not a valid labelled homogeneous copy, or the proposed abstract bound algorithm fails to terminate despite its stated mathematical premises.
scope_boundary: This closes only classical mathematical vertex-pattern forcing. No native derivation of Hales-Jewett, source-history-faithful word encoding, practical two-color tetrahedral/octahedral numeric bound, optimal Ramsey number, graph/hypergraph result or root closure is inferred.
